evidence: Same stale four-representation/.json text as F1 plus two render_pngs.ts sites; e399396 fixes all four and renames captureCellGrids to captureCellRecords, but the sweep did not reach the five other .json comments (F12) or capture-env's 'cell grid' wording (F16).

evidence: The shell loader pushed any non-blank non-# line into env args while capture_python.py raised ValueError on a line with no '='; e399396 adds the matching fatal check. The fix only covered the no-'=' case, which left the whitespace, indentation and EOF differences found in F8/F10/F18.
guidance_note: When two hand-written parsers must agree on one file, list every normalization each one does (strip, split, EOF handling, branch order) and match all of them in one pass, or pin the file to a grammar both trivially agree on.

evidence: The rewritten docstring dropped the 'from the visual-tests directory' requirement and gave 'uv run python capture_python.py', which won't find visual-tests/pyproject.toml from the repo root; e399396 uses the --project form render_pngs.ts actually invokes.
guidance_note: When rewriting a usage line in a docstring, copy the invocation the real caller uses, not a shortened one.

evidence: '**/snapshots/**' excluded every directory named snapshots anywhere, while the rationale only covered visual-tests/snapshots; the agent correctly explained that the dist/** doubling convention doesn't apply to a fully qualified path and dropped the pattern.
guidance_note: Before copying a pattern convention from adjacent code, check that the reason documented for it applies to the new case.

evidence: The F5 fix in e399396 added a no-'=' check so the shell loader would 'fail the same way' as Python, but it left lines untrimmed while Python does line.strip(), so '  FORCE_COLOR=3' passes and becomes a variable literally named '  FORCE_COLOR'. This is the same loader-parity gap that F5 targeted, in a normalization step the fix didn't sweep.
guidance_note: When fixing one divergence between mirrored parsers, diff their full pipelines step by step (trim, comment test, split, key/value strip) instead of patching only the step the reviewer named.

evidence: Flag false positive: the guard regex `${variable}["'\]\s]*=` was in the PR before review (d83f9a5 shows it as the '-' side), and e399396 didn't touch the test. The premise holds because capture_python.py's own os.environ.update({...}) dict-key spelling slips past it; the agent confirmed this by reintroducing it and watching the test fail.
guidance_note: When writing a regex guard against reintroduction, test it against every spelling the guarded files themselves already use, starting with the idiom in the code it protects.

evidence: '${line// }' deletes spaces anywhere, but the '#' test sees the untrimmed line, so '  # note' reaches the KEY=VALUE check that e399396 added for F5 and dies with 'expected KEY=VALUE', while Python's strip() treats it as a comment. This is the same parity gap F5's fix left open.
guidance_note: When fixing one divergence between mirrored parsers, diff their full pipelines step by step (trim, comment test, split, key/value strip) instead of patching only the step the reviewer named.

evidence: Flag false positive: `join(import.meta.dirname, ...)` was in the test's original 'capture environment' block (diff hunk @@ -166,3 +169,48), and e399396 didn't touch it. With engines.node >=18 it is undefined on Node 18; d83f9a5 switched to dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)).

evidence: Flag false positive: `os.environ.pop("NO_COLOR", None)` and `env -u NO_COLOR` were in the original consolidation (visible in the pre-review hunk), not added by e399396. The premise holds because NO_COLOR is a per-path subset that the 'apply this file whole' header forbids; the agent took the reviewer's first option (a -KEY directive), but the new branch spawned F17, F19 and F22.
guidance_note: When a PR declares one file the single source of truth, check whether every per-path setting can actually be expressed in that file's format before claiming consolidation.

evidence: Relocation false positive: 'Gate 4 compares them at AE == 0 far more exactly than a reader can' was already in the pre-review workflow comment, and e399396 moved it verbatim into .github/code-review.conf. The claim is false for .ansi/.txt since compare.ts reads only .png, and the agent verified that before narrowing it in d83f9a5.

evidence: The d83f9a5 fix for F8 trimmed only the whole line, while Python also strips key, value and the -KEY remainder, so 'FORCE_COLOR = 3' and '- NO_COLOR' still diverge. 7ce8ced routes every piece through trim() and adds a grammar test, which is a real single enforcement point for the file format.
guidance_note: When matching another parser's whitespace handling, mirror every .strip() call it makes (line, key, value, removal name), not just the first one.

evidence: The F4 fix in e399396 renamed 'cell grid' to 'cell record' in render_pngs.ts and capture_python.py but left capture-env (a new file in this PR) saying 'cell grid' and 'JSON recorded', and left render-fixture-xvfb.sh saying 'cell grid'. 7ce8ced fixes both.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a terminology rename, grep the old term across the repo and rename every hit in the same commit.

evidence: The F13 fix in d83f9a5 added the '-' removal branch before the '=' validation, storing `stripped[1:].strip()` unchecked, so '-NO_COLOR=1' pops a nonexistent variable without any error. 7ce8ced adds refusal in both loaders.
guidance_note: When adding a new directive form to a validated format, give the new branch the same malformed-input refusal as the existing branch before shipping.

evidence: `while IFS= read -r line` skips an unterminated final line, while Python's splitlines() keeps it. The loop predates review, but it is another parser-parity difference the F5/F8 parity fixes didn't sweep, and d83f9a5 made it acute by putting -NO_COLOR last. 7ce8ced reads via `< <(cat ...; echo)`.
guidance_note: When two parsers must agree, compare their line-reading mechanics (EOF, trailing newline) as well as their per-line logic.

evidence: The F13 fix moved NO_COLOR into capture-env as -NO_COLOR, but the guard regex `[=:]` only catches assignment spellings, so re-adding `os.environ.pop("NO_COLOR", None)` or `env -u NO_COLOR` passes. 7ce8ced adds removal-form patterns keyed off the -KEY directives, and the agent confirmed they fire.
guidance_note: When extending a single-source file with a new directive kind, extend the guard test that protects that file to cover the new kind's reintroduction spellings in the same commit.

evidence: The F14 fix narrowed the 'Gate 4 compares' overclaim in code-review.conf. d83f9a5 also edited the sparkline comment line directly above 'the same ground truth the pixel gate compares against' and carried the overclaim forward. ca68722 rewords it to say the .ansi records the frame the .png comes from.
guidance_note: When a finding shows a claim is false, grep for every restatement of that claim across the repo and correct them all in the same fix.

evidence: Flag false positive: ca68722 only changed a test comment, and the nargs='+' CLI plus the unguarded captureCellRecords(fixtures) call are from the original PR. The agent confirmed that argparse exits with status 2 when no names are given and gated the call on fixtures.length > 0 in 4a6bf5c.
guidance_note: When tightening a CLI to require arguments (nargs='+'), check every caller's empty-list path.

evidence: The -KEY form added for F13 introduced a cross-line conflict: Python updates and then pops, so removal wins, while `env -u ... NAME=VALUE` applies the operand after the -u options, so assignment wins. The per-line grammar test added in 7ce8ced can't see this. 4a6bf5c adds a set-level uniqueness rule to the grammar test.
guidance_note: When adding a second directive kind to a format, define how a name declared in both kinds resolves and enforce it in the same commit.

narrative: The PR consolidated capture env into one file read by two hand-written loaders (shell and Python). Most later findings are parity gaps between those loaders that each fix patched one at a time: F5 → F8/F10 → F15/F18. The rest are gaps in the F13 -KEY directive extension (F17, F19, F22) and stale .json/'cell grid' wording that the F4 sweep missed (F12, F16). Every reviewer premise was correct and every acceptance was justified. Rounds 2 and 3 consisted entirely of fix-caused findings. Round 4 had one independent finding, and round 5 was a cap-hit non-review.
guidance_observations: The agent identified the root cause (two mirrored parsers) only in round 2's issue comment; adding the single-enforcer grammar test when F5 first exposed loader asymmetry would likely have closed F8, F10, F15, F17 and F18 together.
Stale-reference sweeps were done with filename greps rather than extension or term greps, which took two extra findings (F12, F16) to finish.
Each format extension (the -KEY directive) shipped without its validation, guard-test coverage, or cross-directive semantics, producing three follow-up findings from one fix.
The PR hit MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS, so the final fix commit 4a6bf5c merged without review.
